title: Driver
description: Deadline for Applications November 5, 2026 Hardship Level E (most hardship) Family Type Non Family with Residential Location Residential location (if applicable) Addis Ababa,Eth Fed Dem Rep Grade GS2 Staff Member / Affiliate Type General Service Reason Regular > Regular Assignment Target Start Date 2027-01-01 Standard Job Description Driver Organizational Setting and Work Relationships The Driver in the UNHCR Office is normally supervised directly by the Administrative Officer/Associate/Assistant or another staff member when the scale of the Operation so require it. Besides driving, the incumbent is responsible for up keep and maintenance of the assigned UNHCR vehicle(s) as per technical guidance and specifications established by the Organisation. S/he is required to follow strict instructions and security guidance provided by the supervisor. While the basic function of a driver is to drive the official vehicles of UNHCR, s/he may be called upon to perform minor maintenance and repair of UNHCR vehicles. The Driver has regular contacts with staff within the UNHCR Office and with others (including Partners, government authorities, etc.) outside UNHCR involving a limited exchange of information. All UNHCR staff members are accountable to perform their duties as reflected in their job description. They do so within their delegated authorities, in line with the regulatory framework of UNHCR which includes the UN Charter, UN Staff Regulations and Rules, UNHCR Policies and Administrative Instructions as well as relevant accountability frameworks. In addition, staff members are required to discharge their responsibilities in a manner consistent with the core, functional, cross-functional and managerial competencies and UNHCR¿s core values of professionalism, integrity and respect for diversity. Duties - Drive UNHCR vehicles for the transport of authorized passengers, deliver, and collect documents and other items. - Meet official personnel at airports or other locations and facilitate immigration and customs formalities as required. - Perform day-to-day maintenance of the assigned vehicles; check oil, water, battery, brakes, tires, etc. and ensure that the assigned UNHCR vehicles are road or waterway worthy and maintained up to the established security standards. - Perform minor repairs, arrange for other repairs, and ensure that the vehicle is kept clean. - Ensure that the steps required by rules and regulations, or other local procedures, are taken in case of involvement in an accident. - Log official trips, daily mileage, gas consumption, oil changes, greasing, etc. - Ensure that instructions and security guidance provided by the supervisor and security focal point are strictly followed. - Ensures valid documentation for passengers, items or cargo in vehicle. - Support the identification and management of risks and seek to seize opportunities impacting objectives in the area of responsibility. Ensure decision making in risk based in the functional area of work. Raise risks, issues and concerns to a supervisor or to relevant functional colleague(s). - Perform other related duties as required. title: Community-Based Protection Associate
description: Deadline for Applications November 4, 2026 Hardship Level E (most hardship) Family Type Non Family with Residential Location Residential location (if applicable) Addis Ababa,Eth Fed Dem Rep Grade GS6 Staff Member / Affiliate Type General Service Reason Regular > Regular Assignment Target Start Date 2027-01-01 Standard Job Description Community-Based Protection Associate Organizational Setting and Work Relationships The Community-Based Protection Associate is a member of the Protection Unit and may report to the Protection Officer, Community-Based Protection Officer, or another more senior staff member in the Protection Unit. Under the overall direction of the Protection Unit, and in coordination with other UNHCR staff, government, NGO partners and other stakeholders, the Community-Based Protection Associate works directly with communities of concern to identify the risks they face and to leverage their capacities to protect themselves, their families and communities. The incumbent may have direct supervisory responsibility for part of the protection and/or support staff and supports the application of community-based protection standards, operational procedures and practices in community-based protection delivery at the field level. To fulfil this role, the Community-Based Protection Associate is required to spend a substantial percentage of the workday outside the office, building and maintaining networks within communities of PoC. The development and maintenance of constructive relationships with PoC that measurably impact and enhance protection planning, programming and results, form the core of the work of the incumbent. S/he also supports the designing of a community-based protection strategy by ensuring that it is based on consultation with PoC. All UNHCR staff members are accountable to perform their duties as reflected in their job description. They do so within their delegated authorities, in line with the regulatory framework of UNHCR which includes the UN Charter, UN Staff Regulations and Rules, UNHCR Policies and Administrative Instructions as well as relevant accountability frameworks. In addition, staff members are required to discharge their responsibilities in a manner consistent with the core, functional, cross-functional and managerial competencies and UNHCRs core values of professionalism, integrity and respect for diversity. Duties - Assist functional units, the Multi-Functional Team (MFT) and senior management to integrate participatory and community-based approaches in the overall protection strategy and operational procedures. - Through relationships with PoC and network of partners, stay abreast of political, social, economic and cultural developments that have an impact on the protection environment and provide advice to the protection team. Understand the perspectives, capacities, needs and resources of the PoC and advise the protection team accordingly, highlighting the specific protection needs of women and men, children, youth and older persons, persons with disabilities, marginalized groups. - Work with host communities to identify opportunities for national civil society involvement in improving the protection of PoC. - Work with implementing and operational partners as well as with displaced and local communities to develop community-owned activities to address, where applicable, the social, educational, psycho-social, cultural, health, organisational and livelihood concerns as well as child protection and prevention and response to GBV. - Assist in the analysis that identifies the capacities of communities of concern and risks they face. - Support participatory assessments by multifunctional teams and ongoing consultation with PoC. - Assist in planning and monitoring of programmes and budgets, with an AGD perspective - Build office capacity for community-based protection through training and establishing systems for community mobilization and participation of PoC. - Support communities in establishing representation and coordination structures. - Ensure community understanding of UNHCRs commitment to deliver on accountability and quality assurance in its response. - Act as an interpreter in exchange of routine information, contribute to related liaison activities and respond directly to routine queries. - Contribute to the enforcement of participatory AGD sensitive analysis as an essential basis for all of UNHCRs work. - Initiate AGD sensitive interventions at the appropriate level on community-based protection issues and to respond to protection concerns and incidents within the office, with external interlocutors, groups and individuals based on agreed parameters. - Identify and select which individuals or groups to prioritize for counselling and field visits based on agreed criteria. - Intervene with authorities on protection. - Enforce compliance of implementing partners with global protection policies and standards of professional integrity in the delivery of protection services. - Recommend and prepare payments to individual cases. - Support the identification and management of risks and seek to seize opportunities impacting objectives in the area of responsibility. Ensure decision making in risk based in the functional area of work. Raise risks, issues and concerns to a supervisor or to relevant functional colleague(s). - Perform other related duties as required. title: Senior Medical Scientist
description: This position is remote-based. Salary range for US-based candidate is $165,000.00 to $180,000.00. Compensation for this position will be determined by the prevailing market rate in the employee's country and the applicable statutory laws, in addition to Ipas's own pay philosophy and other factors, such as the employee's experience level and expertise. Position may work remotely from any of the following US states: AZ, CA, CO, DC, FL, GA, MD, MA, MI, NJ, NY, NC, PA, SC, TX, VA, WA. Additionally, the position may work remotely from any of the following countries outside of the US: Bangladesh, Bolivia, Canada, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Cote d’Ivoire, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Kenya, Malawi, Mexico, Mozambique, Myanmar, Nepal, Nigeria, South Africa, and Zambia. The Senior Medical Scientist will provide technical leadership to help ensure that the best available evidence supports quality and continuous improvement in safe abortion, contraception, and gender-based violence management across development and humanitarian contexts. This role will strengthen abortion availability, accessibility, acceptability and quality through formal health systems and self-care pathways by establishing and enhancing global technical tools, standards, processes, monitoring mechanisms, and partnerships that contribute to a sustainable abortion ecosystem. Summary of Responsibilities The Senior Medical Scientist is a subject matter expert, using clinical expertise, evolving evidence and strategic partnerships to advance Ipas’s mission at the global level. In collaboration with key staff across the organization, Senior Medical Scientist will advance innovative initiatives and provide strategic guidance and technical assistance on safe abortion, contraception and GBV care quality and access. The Senior Medical Scientist disseminates new evidence through publications and presentations; conducts training; represents Ipas externally, advocating for the organization’s mission within the broader reproductive health field; and builds partnerships with colleague organizations to maximize impact. Organizational Leadership and Strategy: Provides technical leadership to develop and test innovative approaches to improve quality abortion and contraception care (e.g., global quality indicators, quality improvement processes) and to integrate safe abortion and postabortion contraception into SRHR programming for Ipas support programs and in emergency crisis settings Program, technical, or functional content of the job: Provide and/or analyze evidence based technical content used for advocacy opportunities related to safe abortion for Ipas supported programs and external coalitions Develop technical tools and resources translating evidence based clinical updates into health services Provides technical leadership on quality and regulatory processes pertinent to the Ipas MVA product line, as well as infection prevention and MVA processing Supports training of Ipas supported sites and partners on content such as VCAT, clinical management of abortion and contraception care, trauma-informed care, legal risk assessment, etc. Leads and/or significant participation in clinical/technical research and technical evidence dissemination for abortion/contraception clinical practice improvement Prepare and/or analyze service delivery data and issue clinical recommendations for continuous improvement of quality of care across the pathways to care. Resource mobilization: Supports fundraising initiatives by contributing to donor proposals and preparation/review of donor reports Communications & representation: Write periodic evidence summaries for internal communications with technical staff across the network Provides external leadership, Ipas representation, and advocacy as required at national, regional and international conferences and events Disseminates evidence externally through presentations and publications Position Requirements A deep commitment to sexual and reproductive health and rights, especially abortion, contraception and GBV care access Demonstrated contribution to the development of technical tools, standards, guidelines, and SRHR research. Professional-level fluency in English (speaking, reading, and writing) Proven ability to support and strengthen the capacity of teams, including through training, supportive supervision, strong communication, nonhierarchical leadership approaches, and modeling the Ipas core values. Demonstrated capacity and commitment to good stewardship of funds, including strong skills in work planning, budgeting, financial monitoring, and data-driven problem solving. Proven ability to build positive working relationships in a multicultural and complex implementation contexts with diverse internal teams and external partners Education Advanced clinical degree (e.g nursing, midwifery) Experience 10 years’ experience in clinical practice including reproductive health care and experience applying scientific clinical information to practical training and programs Substantive experience with evaluation of quality in clinical care and quality improvement. Substantive knowledge and experience of international reproductive health programs and systems in low-resource and humanitarian settings Knowledge of key partners and influencers in our field Experience working in multicultural teams Preferred Qualifications PhD or DrPH and/or significant experience in research Strong clinical background Experience working in humanitarian contexts and/or working with humanitarian implementing agencies Established relationships with non-profit organizations and advocacy groups Proficiency with at least one Ipas working language, such as French, Portuguese, or Spanish. Strong preference for advanced practice midwife or nurse Working environment: Ability to travel up to 20% of the time internationally, including in crisis settings Ipas is strongly committed to providing a work environment that is free from all forms of harassment, discrimination, and inequity. title: Global Audience Insight & Engagement Advisor
description: This position is remote-based. Salary range for US-based candidate is $65,000.00 to $72,000.00. Compensation for this position will be determined by the prevailing market rate in the employee's country and the applicable statutory laws, in addition to Ipas's own pay philosophy and other factors, such as the employee's experience level and expertise. Position may work remotely from any of the following US states: AZ, CA, CO, DC, FL, GA, MD, MA, MI, NJ, NY, NC, PA, SC, TX, VA, WA. Additionally, the position may work remotely from any of the following countries outside of the US: Bangladesh, Bolivia, Canada, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Cote d’Ivoire, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Kenya, Malawi, Mexico, Mozambique, Myanmar, Nepal, Nigeria, South Africa, and Zambia. The Audience Insights and Engagement Advisor is responsible for using audience insights, measurement, and performance data to strengthen engagement across Ipas’s communications channels, including digital platforms, email, campaigns, publications, events, and other audience-facing initiatives. S/he tracks audience needs, behaviors, and responses; analyzes content and campaign performance; and translates findings into clear recommendations that improve reach, relevance, engagement, and impact. This role helps create, disseminate, monitor, and optimize compelling content and communications approaches based on what priority audiences need, value, and respond to. Working closely with Communications, Development, country teams, and other colleagues, the Advisor helps design audience-informed strategies/tactics and campaigns with measurable objectives, evaluates results, and makes data-informed adjustments that raise awareness, deepen supporter engagement, and support organizational goals. This individual plays a key role in shaping engagement strategies grounded in audience understanding, consistent measurement, and alignment with broader organizational priorities. Primary Responsibilities: Develop and execute audience engagement strategies grounded in audience insights, channel performance, and clear communications goals, coordinating with Communications colleagues to ensure alignment with the overall editorial calendar and organizational priorities. Track and interpret audience behavior, feedback, and engagement across communications channels, including social media, email, web, publications, campaigns, events, and other audience-facing initiatives. Design and maintain reporting systems that measure reach, engagement, conversion, audience growth, message resonance, and campaign effectiveness, translating data into practical recommendations for decision-making. Exercise decision-making authority for routine audience engagement, channel optimization, and performance reporting decisions within approved communications strategies and budgets. Guide country teams in developing audience-informed communications approaches that reflect the Ipas brand and use audience and performance data to inform strategy, message development, and channel choices. Collaborate with Communications and fundraising teams to design campaigns with precise objectives, defined audiences, measurable outcomes, and clear learning and reporting plans. Implement and optimize engagement approaches across paid, earned, shared, and owned channels to distribute content, strengthen relationships, grow priority audiences, and support individual donor engagement. Actively engage with followers, supporters, partners, and stakeholders across platforms Collaborate with the Content Manager, Audience Engagement Specialist, and other colleagues on audience segmentation, message testing, and performance metrics to inform campaign design and content creation. Monitor emerging trends, technologies, audience behaviors, communications practices, and relevant regulations, assessing implications for engagement, measurement, and content strategy. Manage campaign logistics, ensuring adherence to timelines, budgets, reporting expectations, and effective communication with all stakeholders. Present clear, actionable metrics for the CEO Dashboard and other reporting needs, showing the reach, engagement, audience growth, message resonance, and impact of Communications initiatives. Contribute to building the communications and brand ambassadorship capacity of the Ipas network by helping gather feedback on staff needs, sharing audience and performance insights, offering technical assistance as requested, and supporting education, skills-building, and knowledge-sharing activities organized by the Network Communications service node. Performance KPIs: Audience growth and engagement: Demonstrates measurable improvement in priority audience reach, engagement rate, follower or subscriber growth, and meaningful interaction across social, email, web, campaign, event, and publication channels. Insight quality and application: Produces clear audience insights, segmentation findings, test results, and performance analyses that are regularly used to shape content, campaigns, channel choices, and engagement strategies. Campaign performance: Supports campaigns with defined objectives, audiences, timelines, and measurement plans; tracks results such as reach, click-through rate, conversion, content engagement, message resonance, and learning outcomes. Reporting and decision support: Delivers timely, accurate, and actionable reports for the CEO Dashboard and other internal needs, highlighting what is working, what is changing, and what adjustments are recommended. Cross-team collaboration: Builds effective working relationships with Communications, Development, country teams, and other colleagues, ensuring audience insights and performance data are incorporated into shared plans and products. Optimization and learning: Identifies trends, tests new approaches, documents lessons learned and recommends practical improvements that increase communications effectiveness over time. Minimum Requirements: Bachelor’s degree in marketing, communications, digital technology or related field Five years of experience in social/digital marketing and strategic communications in media, non- profit, or agency environment Familiarity with social justice and human rights causes and initiatives Fluency in multiple social media platform management tools and trends Excellent grasp of social media, web and email metrics and best practices (Sprout, Google Analytics, etc.) ExperiencewithMicrosoft OfficeSuite Preferred: Some non-English language fluency Experience in a global nonprofit Graphic design experience Competencies: Proven track record as a collaborative team player who listens, contributes and enjoys teamwork Knowledge of reproductive justice and health messaging Innovative thinker Ipas is strongly committed to providing a work environment that is free from all forms of harassment, discrimination, and inequity. title: Strategic Partnership Manager - Africa
description: This is a remote position. Compensation for this position will be determined by the prevailing market rate in the employee's country in addition to Ipas's own pay philosophy and other factors, such as the employee's experience level and expertise. Candidates based in the following countries are eligible to apply: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Cote d’Ivoire, Ethiopia, Kenya/Alliance locations, Malawi, Mozambique, Nigeria, South Africa, Zambia. Ipas seeks a Strategic Partnership Manager to strengthen resource mobilization and the partnership portfolio in Africa. The manager will identify, cultivate, and expand a pipeline of institutional donors, foundations, corporate partners, and strategic collaborators whose priorities align with Ipas's mission and values. The role will provide targeted business development support for high-value funding opportunities, deepen engagement with priority donors and partners, and contribute to compelling donor-facing materials, including expressions of interest, concept notes, proposals, budgets, presentations, results frameworks, and partnership strategies. The Strategic Partnership Manager will demonstrate a strong commitment to reproductive justice, including human rights, abortion rights, gender equity, diversity, equity, and inclusion. The role will collaborate across the Ipas Network and promote shared leadership, trust, and inclusive, non-hierarchical approaches to learning and collaboration, while supporting effective stewardship of donor resources and adherence to Ipas's mission, values, and standards. Primary Responsibilities: 1. Opportunity Pipeline Development and Donor/Partner Intelligence Map priority foundations, institutional funders, corporate partners, and strategic implementing partners aligned with Ipass mission and work. Analyze funder priorities, eligibility, timelines, typical award size, indirect cost expectations, compliance considerations, and relationship pathways. Identify and track requests for proposals, calls for proposals, invitations, and relationship-led opportunities, and maintain an up-to-date pipeline tracker. Support go/no-go decisions through fit assessments, competitiveness analysis, and risk and feasibility review, including deadlines, staffing, partnership needs, cost share, and indirect rate constraints. 2. External Relations and Resource Mobilization Support Develop donor and partner engagement plans for priority prospects, including objectives, messages, decision-makers, and follow-up actions. Draft and refine positioning materials, including capability statements, one-pagers, brief slide decks, project summaries, and boilerplate language. Build Ipas Network intelligence on key trends and opportunities in Africa. Work with the Communications Service Node to contribute to external communications through the Ipas website, newsletters, and social media. Prepare talking points, briefing notes, and agendas for external meetings; when requested, participate in meetings, capture next steps, and support follow-up. Advise on partnership strategy, including lead versus sub-award roles, consortium roles, negotiation points, partner mapping, and outreach. Work with the Development Service Node to report quarterly and annually on fundraising efforts and results and participate in annual management cycle activities. 3. Proposal Development, Review, and Quality Assurance Support donor-facing submissions, including expressions of interest, concept notes, and full proposals, in coordination with internal teams and partners. Develop and review technical narratives for compliance, clarity, and responsiveness to donor evaluation criteria. Support required annexes, including results frameworks or log frames, workplans, monitoring, evaluation and learning plans, risk matrices, and staffing plans. Coordinate with finance counterparts to develop and quality-check budgets and budget narratives for alignment with the technical approach and donor cost rules. Provide structured written feedback through tracked comments or review memos and participate in review meetings to agree on revisions and next steps. Minimum Requirements: Ten or more years’ work experience managing programs and projects with increasing complexity and responsibility Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field Demonstrated experience in business development, fundraising, and/or proposal development for NGOs, social enterprises, or mission-driven organizations. Strong understanding of institutional donor environments, including bilateral and multilateral agencies, foundations, and partnership or consortium approaches. Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and French. Ability to manage multiple deadlines, coordinate across teams, and deliver high-quality products with minimal supervision. Proven record of developing competitive proposals and donor-facing products, including complex budgets and results frameworks or log frames. Subject-matter expertise in sexual and reproductive health and rights and reproductive justice, and/or experience working internationally. Deep commitment to reproductive justice, human rights, abortion rights, gender equity, diversity, equity, and inclusion. Commitment to shared leadership, trust, and inclusive, non-hierarchical ways of working. Travel & Work Environment Regular travel within Africa and to strategic hubs, in accordance with Ipas travel policies. Virtual collaboration with colleagues across the Ipas Network and across time zones. Weekly written progress updates and biweekly virtual check-ins with the Director of Development and relevant staff. Deliverables submitted electronically in editable formats, such as Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, unless otherwise agreed. Ipas utilizes Workday’s full suite of solutions for Human Capital Management (HCM) and Financial Management, and this role will collaborate closely with their counterpart in HR to ensure data integrity across functional areas. • This role will directly manage and maintain the Workday system. The Workday System Administrator is a skilled communicator, a strong documenter of processes and decisions, and is able to clearly and effectively provide updates on the status of ongoing projects, issues, and upcoming needs. Expertise in the design, implementation, and deployment of user-centric systems, with a focus on usability. Proven record of clear communication (oral and written) with diverse audiences and a record of producing clear documentation. Preferred Skills Workday ERP certifications in Financials, and/or Report Writing. Experience with Adaptive Planning and Workday Grants and Awards. Rich skills and experience with Microsoft solutions especially Excel, PowerPoint. Experience with global systems deployment. Experience with Six Sigma, Agile, and/or other methodologies. Expertise in collaborative technologies including Microsoft solutions (SharePoint, OneDrive, Planner, etc.) and/or other project management tools. title: Program Support Director – Francophone and Lusophone Africa
description: This position is 100% remote. Candidates may work remotely from any of the following countries: Burundi, Chad, Benin, Madagascar, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Cote d’Ivoire, Ethiopia, Kenya/Alliance locations, Malawi, Mozambique, Nigeria, South Africa, and Zambia. Candidates in West Africa are preferred. The Program Support Director (PSD) is a senior leadership position within Ipas’s Global Program Support Team. The PSD serves as strategic thought partner to the Regional Directors (RDs), Country Directors (CDs) and other leaders across the Ipas network, helping strengthen organizational effectiveness, program quality, risk management and leadership capacity. The PSD provides strategic leadership, technical guidance, and operational oversight to 4–5 regional or country programs. This role supervises 3-5 direct reports which include CDs and RDs as well as Senior Program Managers (SPMs), who are part of the global Program Support Team. Reporting to the Deputy Chief Operating Officer (DCOO), the PSD ensures alignment with Ipas strategy and quality standards, donor and award compliance, and risk mitigation. The PSD serves as a bridge between Ipas global teams and regional / country offices, promoting cross learning and providing supportive supervision and thought partnership to country team leaders. The PSD will bring significant team and program leadership experience, cross cultural knowledge, relevant language skills, a focus on user-centered approaches, and a dedication to shared leadership. The job responsibilities include working collaboratively with country program staff to ensure strong program results and strong project and risk management. The PSD provides high level stewardship and serve an “internal control” function with assigned regional and country programs, to ensure compliance with Ipas’s quality standards and as a steward of the Ipas’s global reputation. The position contributes significantly to addressing programmatic challenges and problem solving; ensuring we achieve desired goals, donor satisfaction and compliance with award terms and conditions, strengthening systems to improve value for money, organizational learning; and promoting a positive and empowering work culture. The PSD has a strong commitment to reproductive justice and Ipas’s mission. Demonstrates a strong commitment to the individuals and communities we serve, acting with a sense of urgency and providing candid timely support and guidance to their team and peers. Primary Responsibilities: Strategic Leadership Partner with regional and country leadership to advance organizational priorities, strengthen strategic decision-making, and promote alignment with Ipass mission, values, strategic framework, global standards, policies and shared leadership practices. Support leaders in monitoring organizational, programmatic, and financial performance and in addressing emerging challenges, risks, and opportunities Participate in global strategic initiatives and other organizational development efforts to strengthen the Ipas Network, such as global strategic planning, expanding implementation of shared leadership practices and risk management. Represent Ipas on national or regional Boards of Directors, as needed. Support and provide thought leadership to regional and country leadership in translating organizational strategy into high-quality, contextually relevant program strategies. Program Quality, Stewardship and Support Provide high-level strategic inputs and assistance in project and program management with a focus on addressing challenges and problem solving with assigned regional and country teams. Facilitate periodic reviews with country and regional leaders to strengthen compliance, program quality, organizational learning, and accountability towards Ipas policies and quality standards, donor requirements, local laws and regulations, and standard accounting and business practices. Lead or support special assessments or learning initiatives, as needed. Regional and Country Program Support Serve as a trusted advisor to RDs and CDs, supporting leadership effectiveness, adaptive management, and cross-organizational collaboration Provide supportive supervision and thought partnership with RDs and CDs. Promote strong communication, collaboration, and cross learning among Ipas network technical and support units, and other country programs to strengthen programmatic and operational results. Support RDs, CDs and SPMs in addressing implementation challenges, risk management, and adaptive programming. Contribute to developing/updating and implementing strong regional/country strategic plans as requested, ensuring alignment with the Ipas mission and strategic framework. Provide coaching and support to RDs and CDs in recruiting and developing a high functioning team that practices shared leadership and maintains a positive and effective work culture. Provide strategic input on annual work plans, annual operating budgets, reports, and high-priority deliverables, as requested and needed. Oversee the strengthening of a variety of mechanisms to support a positive and effective work culture, organizational learning, sharing, and peer support across teams. Support start-up, scale-up, and close-out of country programs. Staff Management & Capacity Strengthening Foster a culture of shared leadership, accountability, learning, trust, and inclusion by empowering staff to contribute expertise, exercise leadership, and make informed decisions appropriate to their roles. Provide supportive supervision and manage the performance of direct reports, including RDs, CDs and Program Support Team staff. Support capacity strengthening of regional/country teams in program management, donor compliance and risk management. Promote organizational training and other capacity strengthening efforts as needed. Donor Engagement & Compliance Support RDs and CDs in managing complex donor-funded portfolios by strengthening systems, decision-making, compliance practices, and cross-node coordination. Ensure programs comply with donor requirements and organizational policies. Contribute to resource mobilization efforts by contributing to proposal development, donor briefings, and strategic partnerships as requested and needed. Work with program leaders to ensure that new business efforts and proposals are aligned with the country/region’s strategic plan, Ipas strategic framework, technical excellence and innovation, good stewardship of funding, and optimal cost recovery. Represent Ipas in donor meetings, technical forums, and external engagements as required. Risk Management & Safeguarding Ensure timely identification and mitigation of programmatic, operational, and reputational risks, working with country/regional program leaders. Promote safeguarding, protection from sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA), and ethical programming across all supported programs. Conduct regular reviews and work with country / regional leaders to ensure adherence with organizational policies on safeguarding, gender equality, and inclusion. Guard Ipas interests and reputation through oversight on adherence to policies, performance against the annual operating budget, addressing audit findings and ethical issues, and compliance with donor requirements. Work closely with regional and country leaders and other Ipas units to ensure adequate internal controls to reduce the risk of fraud and mismanagement of funds; Play an internal control function where needed, such as to reduce perceived or actual conflicts of interest. Monitoring, Evaluation, Learning & Accountability (MEL) Promote strong monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning practices across assigned regional and country programs. Support the use of data for decision-making, learning, and program improvement. Encourage documentation of best practices, innovations, and lessons learned across all projects. Minimum Requirements: Essential Commitment to sexual and reproductive health and rights, especially safe abortion and access to contraception, and an understanding of principles, policies, and best practices related to sexual and reproductive health, and related intersectionalities. Knowledge of the issues and context of womens sexual and reproductive health and rights in the Africa region, including demonstrated experience working with NGOs in Africa, preferably having worked in an Ipas implementing country in the West Africa region. Demonstrated commitment to shared leadership principles, with experience fostering distributed leadership, collaboration, accountability, and trust across geographically dispersed teams Proven ability to lead and motivate teams and create a positive work environment through supportive supervision, strong communication and teamwork, and shared leadership approaches, including demonstrated successes in program management, team leadership, strategic planning and problem solving. Proven ability to build and maintain positive working relationships with a variety of partners, including government officials, regional or global donors and partner organizations. Ability to work across cultures and manage complex relationships remotely. Minimum At least 15 years of increasing responsibility in non-profit leadership and program management in the international development or NGO-sector. Minimum of 7 years of senior program leadership experience overseeing multiple country programs and proven ability to provide strategic and technical leadership across diverse country contexts. Strong experience managing donor-funded programs (e.g., bilateral, multilateral, foundations) including budgetary management. Demonstrated experience supporting organizational risk management, compliance monitoring, and implementation of internal control systems Relevant post-graduate degree (e.g., MBA, MIA, MPH). Respect and credibility as an advocate for reproductive health and rights Strong written and verbal communication skills in English. Fluency in French required. Knowledge of Portuguese will be an added advantage and of other local languages will be an asset. Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, PowerPoint, Word, SharePoint, etc. Travel Requirements: Estimated 20 %-25 % time travel t o regional and country programs and regional/global meetings. Compensation for this position will be determined by the prevailing market rate in the employees country and the applicable statutory laws, in addition to Ipass own pay philosophy and other factors, such as the employees experience level and expertise. title: Enterprise Risk Management Analyst
description: This position may work remotely from any of the following countries: Bangladesh, Bolivia, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Cote d’Ivoire, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Kenya/Alliance locations, Malawi, Mexico, Mozambique, Nepal, Nigeria, Pakistan, South Africa, the United Kingdom, and Zambia. Compensation for this position will be determined on the prevailing market rate in the employee's country and the applicable statutory laws, in addition to Ipas's own pay philosophy and other factors, such as the employee's experience level and expertise. The Ipas Network Risk Service Node is responsible for supporting and providing resources in the areas of risk management, safety and security, internal audit, and ethics. The Enterprise Risk Management Analyst plays a critical role in strengthening organizational resilience and accountability for Ipas in these areas. This position provides technical and operational support to the Network Risk function, which oversees enterprise risk management (ERM), safety and security, insurance and risk pooling arrangements, internal audit coordination and ethics. The Enterprise Risk Management Analyst identifies and manages threats to an organization's strategic mission, staff safety, and programmatic impact, especially in areas where complex and/or evolving legal, political, and operational landscapes create higher risk for the organization. In addition, the role supports implementation of the organization’s risk management framework to ensure Ipas can effectively identify, assess, and mitigate risks affecting program delivery, donor compliance, safeguarding commitments, and strategic objectives in diverse and often complex operating environments. Risk Identification & Assessment Conduct risk assessments considering political, regulatory, financial, and reputational factors in global operations. Identify knowledge gaps among staff and partners on risk, reporting, and organizational accountability Develop tracking mechanisms to ensure compliance with policies across all offices. Provide analysis and recommendations to inform risk mitigation plans across country offices and global teams. Collaborate with the Network Risk Director in identifying digital and physical risk indicators, ensuring that these are managed under one unified strategy. Partner with the Network Risk Director and BAM/IT Director to ensure physical security protocols (e.g., office access) align with digital security standards (e.g., server room protection). Risk Monitoring, Data Analysis Maintain and update the enterprise risk register and dashboards, synthesizing operational, financial, and security data while incorporating technical risk summaries provided by the Network Risk Director. Use data visualization tools to communicate complex risk information effectively to non-technical audiences. Prepare risk reports for senior leadership, board committees, and donors, highlighting key exposures and mitigation progress. Ensure risk management practices align with donor requirements, international standards, and local regulations in countries of operation. Collaborate with internal audit and program compliance teams to address risk-based findings. Network and Staff Safety & Security Analyze risk trends across advocacy, funding, and operational areas to inform strategic planning. Create and facilitate a network Community of Practice to strengthen safety and security within Ipas implementing areas and across the Ipas Network. Support teams by collaborating with local HR and Risk contact to coordinate resources such as EAP crisis management when facing adverse safety and/or security concerns. Capacity Building & Awareness Deliver trainings during onboarding, refresher cycles, and targeted learning sessions tailored to diverse audiences and local context. Collaborate with HR, Procurement, IT, and Communications teams to integrate risk and accountability into organizational systems. Other duties as assigned. Minimum Bachelors degree in risk management, Finance, International Development, Public Health, or related field. 5 years’ experience in enterprise risk management, compliance, or internal audit, ideally within NGOs or donor-funded projects. Proven experience creating and leading training programs Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Excellent verbal, auditory, and written communication and stakeholder engagement abilities across diverse cultural contexts and various levels of the organization. Ability to clearly and thoroughly present data through various collection sources (reports, risk registers, risk database) to key stakeholders, either through ad-hoc meetings or regularly scheduled trainings Anticipating needs of the organization and programmatic teams proactively through ongoing research and best practice knowledge Strong integrity and ability to coordinate sensitive matters with discretion, confidentiality, and neutrality. Proficiency in risk management tools and data visualization platforms, such as Power BI. Preferred Skills: Familiarity with reproductive health programs and global advocacy environments is highly desirable. Strong verbal, auditory, and written communication skills in any language that is frequently used by Ipas employees (French, Portuguese, Spanish, Hindi, etc.) Certification in Risk Management Core Competencies Commitment to reproductive justice and gender equity principles. Strategic thinking and ability to connect risk insights to mission-driven objectives. Cultural sensitivity and adaptability in global contexts. High ethical standards and integrity.
